newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - fresh issues abound.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - fresh issues abound.

text.p: Asian debt markets were bustling with a spate of fresh issues on Thursday as major Asian issuers wrap up financial needs amid a favourable interest rate environment.
Looking afield for funds, CITIC Hong Kong launched a 20 billion yen samurai bond. Due on 27 March 2003, the issue pays a coupon of 2.8 percent.
A slew of frequent and cash-hungry Korean issuers continued to flow in for last-minute borrowing this year. Bankers warned that the brisk pace of new Korean issues will cause absorption problems.
The Korea Exchange Bank launched its US$200 milllion floating rate note issue. The one year facility was priced at 99.952 to float at 10 basis points over three-month London Interbank Offered Rate.
The fee is five basis points split evenly between selling concession and management underwriting. Nomura lead managed the deal.
"Asian debt markets are flooded with Korean papers, there is just no more room for such a tightly-priced deal, especially towards the year-end," one banker noted.
Other bankers suggested the lead could eye the U.S and European OECD bankers who might have some appeitite for a one-year "fair-yield" deal.
Broadening its borrowing sources, Korea Long Term Credit Bank, another active issuer, hit the Australian kangaroo market today with a three-year A$125 million floating rate note issue.
The paper was priced at 21 basis points over the 90 day bank bill swap rate (BBSW).
The notes are offered at a discount issue price of 99.973.
Commonwealth Bank of Australia was the lead.
In the pipeline, Kookmin Bank's US$200 million ten-year subordinated floating rate note issue is expected to be put into Asian debt markets next week.
Callable in year five, the issue is priced at par to float at 60 basis points over the six-month London interbank Offered Rate for year one to five and 185 basis points thereafter.
Merrill Lynch and Chase are the leads.
Bankers warned the paper might have limited appeal as some banks are not allowed to take subordinated debt paper.
In other news, a group has been formed for GE Capital Finance's HK$200 million subordinated floating rate note issue.

Rated A by Standard & Poor's, the 10-year issue is priced at par to float at 75 basis points over Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate for year one to year six and 200 basis points from year 6.25 to year 10.
Fee are 100 basis points, split as 60 basis points for selling and 40 basis points for management and underwriting.
The issue is callable three years after payment date and annually thereafter.

Boasting its confidence in the issue, lead manager Merrill Lynch Far East opted to take a lion's share of US$160 million. Co-lead managers, with HK$20 million each, are China Construction Bank and Fuji International Finance.
"The issue has the right market timing," a banker noted. Bankers dying to fill their quotas towards year-end have their eyes firmly fixed on the issue, the banker explained.
"The high-grade, reasonable yield paper" is expected to be snapped up swifly although "it is 10-year and subordinated."
Securities houses are likely to be major end-investors in this deal, a banker commented.
